title: Triangle Publishing Company: Classy, Sam Rosenbaum and Joe Virgis
summary: Classy ran Triangle Publishing from his real estate office with Sam Rosenbaum managing; Rosenbaum wrote lyrics, Virgis and Leclerc melodies.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Yeah. And it was right on grab. Well, in those days, Klessy went into the business, Triangle Publishing Company. That was Klessy.

821 Grab. That's where he had his real estate place, you see. Oh, yeah. And Klessy used to... I wonder he... Triangle... Yeah. You see? Yeah. Klessy published this too. Triangle Publishing Company. That was Klessy.
He went into the publishing business and he published his numbers and mine and different ones.
Did you know Joe Virgis? Oh, he and I were pals. Yeah.
Yeah, Joe and I, we wrote quite a few numbers together.
I mean, Sam Rosenbaum. Oh, Sam too.
Well, Sam was the manager of the Triangle Publishing Company. Klessy owned it. But Sam Rosenbaum was the manager.
Yeah, that's what Sam did. That's why I guess you have all these numbers here. Yeah. Well, what did he write?
Words or music, Sam? Do you remember?
Sam, words. He wrote all the lyrics of words. He didn't play the piano or anything like that. He didn't write the melodies at all. Virgis and I used to write the melodies.
And I can't remember Klessy writing too many numbers after he wrote that big hit. Wasn't that a strange thing? One of the few numbers he ever wrote had to be a big, big hit.
I don't know of anything he wrote other than... No. Sorry, I made you cry. Sorry, I made you cry.
Wasn't that funny? Yeah. Joe? Fortunately, he ever wrote had to be a big hit and it brought him a tremendous amount of money.
